252	    async def compute_score_disrm(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
253	        disrm_prompt = await self._preprocess_reward_inputs(data)
254	        engine_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.rollout.name
255	        model_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.model_path
256	        if engine_name == "vllm":
257	            payloads = {
258	                "model": model_name,
259	                "input": disrm_prompt,
260	                "use_activation": False,
261	            }
262	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "classify")
263	            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["probs"][-1]
264	        elif engine_name == "sglang":
265	            payloads = {
266	                "model": model_name,
267	                "input": disrm_prompt,
268	            }
269	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/embeddings")
270	            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["embedding"][-1]
271	        elif engine_name == "trtllm":
272	            # TODO: remove this once TRT-LLM switches to TorchSampler
273	            raise ValueError("TensorRT-LLM backend does not support reward models currently.")
274	
275	            payloads = {
276	                "model": model_name,
277	                "prompt": disrm_prompt,
278	                "return_context_logits": True,
279	            }
280	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/completions")
281	            rm_score = output["choices"][0]["context_logits"]
282	            assert isinstance(rm_score, list) and len(rm_score) > 0, (
283	                "TensorRT-LLM OpenAI server response for reward score is not in the expected format."
284	            )
285	
286	            rm_score = float(rm_score[0][0])
287	            logger.debug(f"rm score: {rm_score}")
288	        else:
289	            raise NotImplementedError(f"RewardLoopManager does not support {engine_name}")
290	
291	        return {"reward_score": rm_score}

294	class RewardLoopManager:
295	    """
296	    RewardLoopManager run in single controller.
297	    This class will create reward loop workers and manage them.
298	    """
299	
300	    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, rm_resource_pool: RayResourcePool = None):
301	        self.config = config
302	        if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
303	            self.reward_model_manager = RewardModelManager(config.reward.reward_model, rm_resource_pool)
304	            self.reward_router_address = self.reward_model_manager.get_router_address()
305	        else:
306	            self.reward_model_manager = None
307	            self.reward_router_address = None
308	
309	        self.reward_loop_workers_class = ray.remote(RewardLoopWorker)
310	        self._init_reward_loop_workers()
311	
312	    @property
313	    def reward_loop_worker_handles(self) -> list[ActorHandle]:
314	        """Return worker handles for agent loop worker to compute reward score.
315	
316	        Only return worker handles when reward computation can be parallelized with rollout:
317	        (1) rule-based reward without reward model
318	        (2) reward model with extra resource pool
319	        """
320	        if not self.config.reward.reward_model.enable or self.config.reward.reward_model.enable_resource_pool:
321	            return self.reward_loop_workers
322	        return None
323	
324	    def _init_reward_loop_workers(self):
325	        self.reward_loop_workers = []
326	        num_workers = self.config.reward.num_workers
327	        node_ids = [node["NodeID"] for node in ray.nodes() if node["Alive"] and node["Resources"].get("CPU", 0) > 0]
328	
329	        for i in range(num_workers):
330	            # Round-robin scheduling over the all nodes
331	            node_id = node_ids[i % len(node_ids)]
332	
333	            self.reward_loop_workers.append(
334	                self.reward_loop_workers_class.options(
335	                    name=f"reward_loop_worker_{i}",
336	                    scheduling_strategy=ray.util.scheduling_strategies.NodeAffinitySchedulingStrategy(
337	                        node_id=node_id,
338	                        soft=True,
339	                    ),
340	                ).remote(self.config, self.reward_router_address)
341	            )
342	
343	    def compute_rm_score(self, data: DataProto) -> DataProto:
344	        if self.reward_model_manager is not None:
345	            self.reward_model_manager.wake_up()
346	
347	        chunks = data.chunk(len(self.reward_loop_workers))
348	        outputs = ray.get(
349	            [
350	                worker.compute_score_batch.remote(chunk)
351	                for worker, chunk in zip(self.reward_loop_workers, chunks, strict=True)
352	            ]
353	        )
354	        outputs_flat = [item for sublist in outputs for item in sublist]
355	
356	        # compute rm score
357	        scores = [item["reward_score"] for item in outputs_flat]
358	        if self.config.reward.reward_manager.name == "visual":
359	            # visual reward only has one score for the whole response
360	            rm_scores = torch.tensor(scores, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(-1)
361	        else:
362	            prompt_length = data.batch["prompts"].size(1)
363	            valid_response_length = data.batch["attention_mask"][:, prompt_length:].sum(dim=1)
364	            rm_scores = torch.zeros_like(data.batch["responses"], dtype=torch.float32)
365	            rm_scores[torch.arange(rm_scores.size(0)), valid_response_length - 1] = torch.tensor(
366	                scores, dtype=torch.float32
367	            )
368	        batch = TensorDict({"rm_scores": rm_scores}, batch_size=len(data))
369	
370	        reward_extra_infos = [output.get("reward_extra_info", {}) for output in outputs_flat]
371	        reward_extra_keys = list(reward_extra_infos[0].keys())
372	        non_tensor_batch = {}
373	        for key in reward_extra_keys:
374	            non_tensor_batch[key] = np.array([info[key] for info in reward_extra_infos])
375	
376	        if self.reward_model_manager is not None:
377	            self.reward_model_manager.sleep()
378	
379	        return DataProto(
380	            batch=batch, non_tensor_batch=non_tensor_batch, meta_info={"reward_extra_keys": reward_extra_keys}
381	        )
382	
383	    def _run_all(self, tasks: list[asyncio.Task]):
384	        async def run_all():
385	            return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
386	
387	        return asyncio.run(run_all())

import asyncio
import logging
import os

import aiohttp
import numpy as np
import ray
import torch
from omegaconf import DictConfig, open_dict
from PIL import Image
from ray.actor import ActorHandle
from tensordict import TensorDict

from verl.protocol import DataProto
from verl.single_controller.ray.base import RayResourcePool
from verl.trainer.ppo.reward import load_reward_manager
from verl.utils import hf_tokenizer
from verl.utils.experimental.reward_utils import pil_image_to_base64, prepare_query_for_multi_modal
from verl.utils.fs import copy_to_local
from verl.utils.ray_utils import get_event_loop

from .reward_model import RewardModelManager

logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)
logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))


def migrate_legacy_reward_impl(config):
    """
    Migrate the legacy reward model implementation to the new one.
    """
    # 1. reward workers migration
    # config.reward_model.num_workers -> config.reward.num_workers
    if config.reward_model.num_workers is not None:
        config.reward.num_workers = config.reward_model.num_workers

    # 2. reward manager migration
    # config.reward_model.reward_manager -> config.reward.reward_manager
    if config.reward_model.reward_manager is not None:
        config.reward.reward_manager.name = config.reward_model.reward_manager
    if config.reward_model.reward_loop_source is not None:
        config.reward.reward_manager.source = config.reward_model.reward_loop_source
        config.reward.reward_manager.module.path = config.reward_model.reward_loop_module_path
        config.reward.reward_manager.module.name = config.reward_model.reward_loop_class_name

    # 3. custom reward function migration
    # config.custom_reward_function -> config.reward.custom_reward_function
    if not all(v is None for v in config.custom_reward_function.values()):
        config.reward.custom_reward_function = config.custom_reward_function

    # 4. reward model migration
    # config.reward_model -> config.reward.reward_model
    for key in ["enable", "enable_resource_pool", "n_gpus_per_node", "nnodes"]:
        if config.reward_model.get(key) is not None:
            config.reward.reward_model[key] = config.reward_model[key]
    if config.reward_model.model.path is not None:
        config.reward.reward_model.model_path = config.reward_model.model.path
    # config.reward_model.reward_kwargs -> config.reward.reward_kwargs (for dapo algo)
    if config.reward_model.get("reward_kwargs") is not None:
        with open_dict(config.reward):
            config.reward["reward_kwargs"] = config.reward_model["reward_kwargs"]
    # config.reward_model.rollout -> config.reward.reward_model.rollout
    legacy_rollout = config.reward_model.rollout
    for key in legacy_rollout.keys():
        if legacy_rollout[key] is not None:
            config.reward.reward_model.rollout[key] = legacy_rollout[key]

    # 5. sandbox_fusion migration
    # config.sandbox_fusion -> reward.sandbox_fusion
    if not all(v is None for v in config.sandbox_fusion.values()):
        config.reward.sandbox_fusion = config.sandbox_fusion

    # 6. delete legacy config from configs
    with open_dict(config):
        del config.reward_model
        del config.custom_reward_function
        del config.sandbox_fusion

    return config


class RewardLoopWorker:
    """
    RewardLoopWork can tackle reward computation:
    (1) rule-based reward computation
    (2) reward model-based reward computation (both disrm and genrm)
    (3) high-flexible user-customized reward function (can access rm by posting requests to reward_model_router)

    Reward Computation Logic:
    - if user-customized reward function is provided:
        -> directly use user-customized reward function
    - if user-customized reward function is not provided:
        -> rm is not enabled: use default rule-based reward function
        -> rm is disrm: compute reward score using disrm
        -> rm is genrm: raise error (user-costomized reward func must be provided)
    """

    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, reward_router_address: str = None):
        """
        Args:
            config: DictConfig, the config for reward loop worker.
            reward_router_address: str, the address of reward router.
        """
        self.config = config
        self.reward_router_address = reward_router_address
        self._init_reward_fn()
        self.loop = get_event_loop()

    def _init_reward_fn(self):
        input_tokenizer_path = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.model.tokenizer_path
        if input_tokenizer_path is None:
            input_tokenizer_path = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path
        input_tokenizer_local_path = copy_to_local(input_tokenizer_path)
        self.input_tokenizer = hf_tokenizer(input_tokenizer_local_path, trust_remote_code=True)
        self.reward_model_tokenizer = None
        if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
            reward_model_tokenizer_local_path = copy_to_local(self.config.reward.reward_model.model_path)
            self.reward_model_tokenizer = hf_tokenizer(reward_model_tokenizer_local_path, trust_remote_code=True)

        self.reward_manager = load_reward_manager(
            self.config,
            self.input_tokenizer,
            reward_router_address=self.reward_router_address,
            reward_model_tokenizer=self.reward_model_tokenizer,
        )

    async def compute_score_batch(self, data: DataProto) -> list[dict]:
        tasks = []
        for i in range(len(data)):
            tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self.compute_score(data[i : i + 1])))
        outputs = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
        return outputs

    async def compute_score(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
        assert len(data) == 1, "RewardLoopWorker only support single data item"
        if self.config.reward.custom_reward_function.path is not None:
            # directly use user-customized reward function
            return await self.reward_manager.run_single(data)
        else:
            if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
                # we assume the rm is disrm
                # genrm must set custom_reward_function
                return await self.compute_score_disrm(data)
            else:
                return await self.reward_manager.run_single(data)

    async def _post_request(self, payload: dict, endpoint: str, max_retries: int = 16):
        url = f"http://{self.reward_router_address}/{endpoint}"
        last_exception = None
        for attempt in range(max_retries):
            try:
                # It's safer to have a timeout instead of None, which can hang indefinitely.
                timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=None)
                async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout) as session:
                    async with session.post(url, json=payload) as resp:
                        resp.raise_for_status()
                        return await resp.json()
            except aiohttp.ClientResponseError as e:
                # Do not retry on 4xx client errors, but retry on 5xx server errors.
                if 400 <= e.status < 500:
                    logger.error(f"Request to {url} failed with client error HTTP {e.status}: {e}. Not retrying.")
                    raise
                last_exception = e
                logger.warning(
                    f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed with HTTP {e.status}: {e}. "
                    "Retrying..."
                )
            except (asyncio.TimeoutError, aiohttp.ClientConnectorError) as e:
                last_exception = e
                logger.warning(f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed: {e}. Retrying...")
            except Exception as e:
                last_exception = e
                logger.warning(
                    f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed with unexpected error: {e}. "
                    "Retrying..."
                )

            if attempt < max_retries - 1:
                # Using exponential backoff is generally better than a fixed sleep.
                backoff_seconds = 2**attempt
                await asyncio.sleep(min(backoff_seconds, 30))

        logger.error(f"Max retries ({max_retries}) reached for request to {url}.")
        if last_exception:
            raise last_exception

    async def _preprocess_reward_inputs(self, data: DataProto) -> str:
        assert len(data) == 1, "RewardLoopWorker only support single data item"
        data_item = data[0]
        assert "raw_prompt" in data_item.non_tensor_batch

        # extract raw prompt
        chat: list = list(data_item.non_tensor_batch["raw_prompt"])

        # extract response
        response = data_item.batch["responses"]
        if response.ndim == 3:
            # handling multi-modal response
            response_image = response
            if isinstance(response_image, torch.Tensor):
                response_image = response_image.float().permute(1, 2, 0).cpu().numpy()
            assert response_image.shape[-1] == 3, "must be in HWC format"
            response_image = (response_image * 255).round().clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
            response_image = Image.fromarray(response_image)

            image_base64 = await self.loop.run_in_executor(None, pil_image_to_base64, response_image)
            query = prepare_query_for_multi_modal(image_base64)

            chat.append({"role": "assistant", "content": query})
        else:
            response_ids = response
            response_length = response_ids.shape[-1]
            valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][-response_length:].sum()
            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

            # decode
            rollout_response = self.input_tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids)
            # remove bos and eos
            rollout_response = rollout_response.replace(self.input_tokenizer.eos_token, "")

            chat.append({"role": "assistant", "content": rollout_response})

        rm_prompt = self.reward_model_tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            chat,
            add_generation_prompt=False,
            tokenize=False,
        )

        # llama tokenizer will add bos token by default
        # will be removed in vllm >= 0.11.2, where we can add "add_special_tokens" = False
        if self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token is not None and rm_prompt.startswith(
            self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token
        ):
            rm_prompt = rm_prompt[len(self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token) :]

        return rm_prompt

    async def compute_score_disrm(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
        disrm_prompt = await self._preprocess_reward_inputs(data)
        engine_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.rollout.name
        model_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.model_path
        if engine_name == "vllm":
            payloads = {
                "model": model_name,
                "input": disrm_prompt,
                "use_activation": False,
            }
            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "classify")
            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["probs"][-1]
        elif engine_name == "sglang":
            payloads = {
                "model": model_name,
                "input": disrm_prompt,
            }
            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/embeddings")
            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["embedding"][-1]
        elif engine_name == "trtllm":
            # TODO: remove this once TRT-LLM switches to TorchSampler
            raise ValueError("TensorRT-LLM backend does not support reward models currently.")

            payloads = {
                "model": model_name,
                "prompt": disrm_prompt,
                "return_context_logits": True,
            }
            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/completions")
            rm_score = output["choices"][0]["context_logits"]
            assert isinstance(rm_score, list) and len(rm_score) > 0, (
                "TensorRT-LLM OpenAI server response for reward score is not in the expected format."
            )

            rm_score = float(rm_score[0][0])
            logger.debug(f"rm score: {rm_score}")
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError(f"RewardLoopManager does not support {engine_name}")

        return {"reward_score": rm_score}


class RewardLoopManager:
    """
    RewardLoopManager run in single controller.
    This class will create reward loop workers and manage them.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, rm_resource_pool: RayResourcePool = None):
        self.config = config
        if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
            self.reward_model_manager = RewardModelManager(config.reward.reward_model, rm_resource_pool)
            self.reward_router_address = self.reward_model_manager.get_router_address()
        else:
            self.reward_model_manager = None
            self.reward_router_address = None

        self.reward_loop_workers_class = ray.remote(RewardLoopWorker)
        self._init_reward_loop_workers()

    @property
    def reward_loop_worker_handles(self) -> list[ActorHandle]:
        """Return worker handles for agent loop worker to compute reward score.

        Only return worker handles when reward computation can be parallelized with rollout:
        (1) rule-based reward without reward model
        (2) reward model with extra resource pool
        """
        if not self.config.reward.reward_model.enable or self.config.reward.reward_model.enable_resource_pool:
            return self.reward_loop_workers
        return None

    def _init_reward_loop_workers(self):
        self.reward_loop_workers = []
        num_workers = self.config.reward.num_workers
        node_ids = [node["NodeID"] for node in ray.nodes() if node["Alive"] and node["Resources"].get("CPU", 0) > 0]

        for i in range(num_workers):
            # Round-robin scheduling over the all nodes
            node_id = node_ids[i % len(node_ids)]

            self.reward_loop_workers.append(
                self.reward_loop_workers_class.options(
                    name=f"reward_loop_worker_{i}",
                    scheduling_strategy=ray.util.scheduling_strategies.NodeAffinitySchedulingStrategy(
                        node_id=node_id,
                        soft=True,
                    ),
                ).remote(self.config, self.reward_router_address)
            )

    def compute_rm_score(self, data: DataProto) -> DataProto:
        if self.reward_model_manager is not None:
            self.reward_model_manager.wake_up()

        chunks = data.chunk(len(self.reward_loop_workers))
        outputs = ray.get(
            [
                worker.compute_score_batch.remote(chunk)
                for worker, chunk in zip(self.reward_loop_workers, chunks, strict=True)
            ]
        )
        outputs_flat = [item for sublist in outputs for item in sublist]

        # compute rm score
        scores = [item["reward_score"] for item in outputs_flat]
        if self.config.reward.reward_manager.name == "visual":
            # visual reward only has one score for the whole response
            rm_scores = torch.tensor(scores, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(-1)
        else:
            prompt_length = data.batch["prompts"].size(1)
            valid_response_length = data.batch["attention_mask"][:, prompt_length:].sum(dim=1)
            rm_scores = torch.zeros_like(data.batch["responses"], dtype=torch.float32)
            rm_scores[torch.arange(rm_scores.size(0)), valid_response_length - 1] = torch.tensor(
                scores, dtype=torch.float32
            )
        batch = TensorDict({"rm_scores": rm_scores}, batch_size=len(data))

        reward_extra_infos = [output.get("reward_extra_info", {}) for output in outputs_flat]
        reward_extra_keys = list(reward_extra_infos[0].keys())
        non_tensor_batch = {}
        for key in reward_extra_keys:
            non_tensor_batch[key] = np.array([info[key] for info in reward_extra_infos])

        if self.reward_model_manager is not None:
            self.reward_model_manager.sleep()

        return DataProto(
            batch=batch, non_tensor_batch=non_tensor_batch, meta_info={"reward_extra_keys": reward_extra_keys}
        )

    def _run_all(self, tasks: list[asyncio.Task]):
        async def run_all():
            return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

        return asyncio.run(run_all())

from __future__ import annotations

import inspect
import multiprocessing
from functools import partial
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Optional, cast

from verl import DataProto
from verl.utils.reward_score import get_default_compute_score

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from omegaconf import DictConfig

    from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager.base import RawRewardFn, RewardManagerBase
    from verl.trainer.config.config import ModuleConfig
    from verl.workers.config.reward import RewardManagerConfig


def _call_with_kwargs(raw_fn, extra_kwargs, *args, **kwargs):
    """Calls `raw_fn` by merging `extra_kwargs` into call-time `kwargs`, with `extra_kwargs` taking precedence.

    This function is used to merge additional keyword arguments with the original function's arguments.
    """
    merged_kwargs = {**kwargs, **extra_kwargs}
    return raw_fn(*args, **merged_kwargs)


async def _call_with_kwargs_async(raw_fn, extra_kwargs, *args, **kwargs):
    """Calls `raw_fn` by merging `extra_kwargs` into call-time `kwargs`, with `extra_kwargs` taking precedence.

    This function is used to merge additional keyword arguments with the original function's arguments.
    """
    merged_kwargs = {**kwargs, **extra_kwargs}
    return await raw_fn(*args, **merged_kwargs)


def get_custom_reward_fn(config: DictConfig) -> Optional[RawRewardFn]:
    """Load and return a custom reward function from external file.

    Dynamically imports a reward function from a specified file path and wraps
    it with additional keyword arguments from the configuration.

    Args:
        config (dict): Configuration dictionary containing custom_reward_function
                      settings with 'path', 'name', and 'reward_kwargs' fields.

    Returns:
        callable or None: Wrapped reward function with merged kwargs, or None
                         if no custom reward function is configured.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the specified reward function file doesn't exist.
        RuntimeError: If there's an error loading the module from file.
        AttributeError: If the specified function name isn't found in the module.
    """

    reward_fn_config = config.reward.get("custom_reward_function") or {}
    module_path = reward_fn_config.get("path")
    if not module_path:
        return None

    fn_name = reward_fn_config.get("name")
    assert fn_name is not None

    from verl.utils.import_utils import load_extern_object

    raw_fn = load_extern_object(module_path=module_path, object_name=fn_name)

    reward_kwargs = dict(reward_fn_config.get("reward_kwargs", {}))
    if not inspect.iscoroutinefunction(raw_fn):
        return partial(_call_with_kwargs, raw_fn, reward_kwargs)
    else:
        return partial(_call_with_kwargs_async, raw_fn, reward_kwargs)


def load_reward_manager(config: DictConfig, tokenizer: Any, **reward_kwargs: Any) -> RewardManagerBase:
    """
    Load and initialize a reward manager based on the configuration.

    Args:
        config: PPO trainer configuration object containing reward_model fields.
        tokenizer: Tokenizer object used for processing text.
        **reward_kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for the reward manager.

    Returns:
        An instance of the specified reward manager class.
    """

    # Try to get a custom reward function based on the configuration
    # user defined reward manager can be registered in custom_reward_fn
    compute_score = get_custom_reward_fn(config)
    final_compute_score = compute_score

    reward_manager_cfg: RewardManagerConfig = config.reward.reward_manager
    reward_manager_cls: type[RewardManagerBase]
    if reward_manager_cfg.source == "register":
        from verl.experimental.reward_loop.reward_manager import get_reward_manager_cls

        reward_manager_cls = get_reward_manager_cls(reward_manager_cfg.name)
    elif reward_manager_cfg.source == "importlib":
        from verl.utils.import_utils import load_extern_object

        module_cfg: ModuleConfig | None = reward_manager_cfg.module
        assert module_cfg is not None and module_cfg.path is not None, (
            f"Module path is required when {reward_manager_cfg.source=}, but got {module_cfg=}"
        )
        reward_manager_cls_name = reward_manager_cfg.name
        reward_manager_cls = cast(
            "type[RewardManagerBase]",
            load_extern_object(module_path=module_cfg.path, object_name=reward_manager_cls_name),
        )

    default_compute_score_ = get_default_compute_score(reward_manager_cfg.name)

    if compute_score is None:
        sandbox_config = config.reward.get("sandbox_fusion")
        sandbox_url = sandbox_config.get("url") if sandbox_config else None
        memory_limit_mb = sandbox_config.get("memory_limit_mb", 1024) if sandbox_config else 1024
        if sandbox_url:
            sandbox_manager = multiprocessing.Manager()
            # Create a semaphore to control concurrent access to the sandbox
            _concurrent_semaphore = sandbox_manager.Semaphore(sandbox_config.get("max_concurrent", 64))
            final_compute_score = partial(
                default_compute_score_,
                sandbox_fusion_url=sandbox_url,
                concurrent_semaphore=_concurrent_semaphore,
                memory_limit_mb=memory_limit_mb,
            )
        else:
            final_compute_score = default_compute_score_

    # Instantiate and return the reward manager with the specified parameters
    return reward_manager_cls(
        config=config,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        compute_score=final_compute_score,
        **reward_kwargs,
    )


def extract_reward(batch: DataProto):
    """
    Extract reward tensor and extra info from batch data.
    """
    reward_tensor = batch.batch["rm_scores"]
    reward_extra_keys = batch.meta_info.get("reward_extra_keys", [])
    reward_extra_infos_dict = {key: batch.non_tensor_batch[key] for key in reward_extra_keys}
    return reward_tensor, reward_extra_infos_dict

27	def calculate_workload(seqlen_list: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
28	    """Calculate approximate computational workload for transformer attention.
29	
30	    Estimates FLOPs for dense transformer blocks based on sequence length using
31	    the formula: FLOPs ≈ 12 * hidden_size² * seqlen + 2 * hidden_size * seqlen²
32	
33	    The constants are calibrated for a 7B model (hidden_size=4096), yielding:
34	    workload ∝ 24576 * seqlen + seqlen²
35	
36	    Args:
37	        seqlen_list: Sequence lengths as a tensor.
38	
39	    Returns:
40	        torch.Tensor: Estimated workload values proportional to actual FLOPs.
41	
42	    Note:
43	        The returned values are relative workloads, not actual FLOP counts.
44	        Useful for balancing computation across data parallel ranks.
45	    """
46	    return 24576 * seqlen_list + seqlen_list**2

49	def karmarkar_karp(seqlen_list: list[int], k_partitions: int, equal_size: bool) -> list[list[int]]:
50	    """Partition items into k groups using the Karmarkar-Karp differencing method.
51	
52	    Implements the Largest Differencing Method (LDM) algorithm for balanced
53	    multi-way number partitioning. This heuristic produces near-optimal partitions
54	    by iteratively combining the sets with the largest difference.
55	
56	    Args:
57	        seqlen_list: Values to partition (typically sequence lengths or workloads).
58	        k_partitions: Number of partitions to create.
59	        equal_size: If True, each partition will have exactly len(seqlen_list) / k_partitions
60	            items. If False, partitions may have different sizes.
61	
62	    Returns:
63	        list[list[int]]: List of k partitions, each containing indices into seqlen_list.
64	
65	    See Also:
66	        https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largest_differencing_method
67	
68	    Note:
69	        When equal_size=True, len(seqlen_list) must be divisible by k_partitions.
70	    """
71	
72	    # see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largest_differencing_method
73	    class Set:
74	        def __init__(self) -> None:
75	            self.sum = 0
76	            self.items = []
77	
78	        def add(self, idx: int, val: int):
79	            self.items.append((idx, val))
80	            self.sum += val
81	
82	        def merge(self, other):
83	            for idx, val in other.items:
84	                self.items.append((idx, val))
85	                self.sum += val
86	
87	        def __lt__(self, other):
88	            if self.sum != other.sum:
89	                return self.sum < other.sum
90	            if len(self.items) != len(other.items):
91	                return len(self.items) < len(other.items)
92	            return self.items < other.items
93	
94	    class State:
95	        def __init__(self, items: list[tuple[int, int]], k: int) -> None:
96	            self.k = k
97	            # sets should always be decreasing order
98	            self.sets = [Set() for _ in range(k)]
99	            assert len(items) in [1, k], f"{len(items)} not in [1, {k}]"
100	            for i, (idx, seqlen) in enumerate(items):
101	                self.sets[i].add(idx=idx, val=seqlen)
102	            self.sets = sorted(self.sets, reverse=True)
103	
104	        def get_partitions(self):
105	            partitions = []
106	            for i in range(len(self.sets)):
107	                cur_partition = []
108	                for idx, _ in self.sets[i].items:
109	                    cur_partition.append(idx)
110	                partitions.append(cur_partition)
111	            return partitions
112	
113	        def merge(self, other):
114	            for i in range(self.k):
115	                self.sets[i].merge(other.sets[self.k - 1 - i])
116	            self.sets = sorted(self.sets, reverse=True)
117	
118	        @property
119	        def spread(self) -> int:
120	            return self.sets[0].sum - self.sets[-1].sum
121	
122	        def __lt__(self, other):
123	            # least heap, let the state with largest spread to be popped first,
124	            # if the spread is the same, let the state who has the largest set
125	            # to be popped first.
126	            if self.spread != other.spread:
127	                return self.spread > other.spread
128	            return self.sets[0] > other.sets[0]
129	
130	        def __repr__(self) -> str:
131	            repr_str = "["
132	            for i in range(self.k):
133	                if i > 0:
134	                    repr_str += ","
135	                repr_str += "{"
136	                for j, (_, seqlen) in enumerate(self.sets[i].items):
137	                    if j > 0:
138	                        repr_str += ","
139	                    repr_str += str(seqlen)
140	                repr_str += "}"
141	            repr_str += "]"
142	            return repr_str
143	
144	    sorted_seqlen_list = sorted([(seqlen, i) for i, seqlen in enumerate(seqlen_list)])
145	    states_pq = []
146	    if equal_size:
147	        assert len(seqlen_list) % k_partitions == 0, f"{len(seqlen_list)} % {k_partitions} != 0"
148	        for offset in range(0, len(sorted_seqlen_list), k_partitions):
149	            items = []
150	            for i in range(k_partitions):
151	                seqlen, idx = sorted_seqlen_list[offset + i]
152	                items.append((idx, seqlen))
153	            heapq.heappush(states_pq, State(items=items, k=k_partitions))
154	    else:
155	        for seqlen, idx in sorted_seqlen_list:
156	            heapq.heappush(states_pq, State(items=[(idx, seqlen)], k=k_partitions))
157	
158	    while len(states_pq) > 1:
159	        state0 = heapq.heappop(states_pq)
160	        state1 = heapq.heappop(states_pq)
161	        # merge states
162	        state0.merge(state1)
163	        heapq.heappush(states_pq, state0)
164	
165	    final_state = states_pq[0]
166	    partitions = final_state.get_partitions()
167	    if equal_size:
168	        for i, partition in enumerate(partitions):
169	            assert len(partition) * k_partitions == len(seqlen_list), (
170	                f"{len(partition)} * {k_partitions} != {len(seqlen_list)}"
171	            )
172	    return partitions

175	def greedy_partition(seqlen_list: list[int], k_partitions: int, equal_size: bool) -> list[list[int]]:
176	    """Partition items into k groups using a greedy assignment strategy.
177	
178	    Assigns each item to the partition with the smallest current sum, iterating
179	    through items in order. Simpler but typically less optimal than Karmarkar-Karp.
180	
181	    Args:
182	        seqlen_list: Values to partition (typically sequence lengths or workloads).
183	        k_partitions: Number of partitions to create.
184	        equal_size: If True, adds a bias to ensure equal partition sizes.
185	            Requires len(seqlen_list) to be divisible by k_partitions.
186	
187	    Returns:
188	        list[list[int]]: List of k partitions, each containing indices into seqlen_list.
189	
190	    Note:
191	        When equal_size=True, a large bias is added to encourage equal distribution
192	        of items before considering the actual values.
193	    """
194	    bias = sum(seqlen_list) + 1 if equal_size else 0
195	    sorted_seqlen = [(seqlen + bias, i) for i, seqlen in enumerate(seqlen_list)]
196	    partitions = [[] for _ in range(k_partitions)]
197	    partition_sums = [0 for _ in range(k_partitions)]
198	    for seqlen, i in sorted_seqlen:
199	        min_idx = None
200	        for j in range(k_partitions):
201	            if min_idx is None or partition_sums[j] < partition_sums[min_idx]:
202	                min_idx = j
203	        partitions[min_idx].append(i)
204	        partition_sums[min_idx] += seqlen
205	    if equal_size:
206	        for i, partition in enumerate(partitions):
207	            assert len(partition) * k_partitions == len(seqlen_list), (
208	                f"{len(partition)} * {k_partitions} != {len(seqlen_list)}"
209	            )
210	    return partitions

213	def get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(seqlen_list: list[int], k_partitions: int, equal_size: bool):
214	    """
215	    Calculates partitions of indices from seqlen_list such that the sum of sequence lengths
216	    in each partition is balanced. Uses the Karmarkar-Karp differencing method.
217	
218	    This is useful for balancing workload across devices or batches, especially when
219	    dealing with variable sequence lengths.
220	
221	    Args:
222	        seqlen_list (List[int]): A list of sequence lengths for each item.
223	        k_partitions (int): The desired number of partitions.
224	        equal_size (bool): If True, ensures that each partition has the same number of items.
225	                           Requires len(seqlen_list) to be divisible by k_partitions.
226	                           If False, partitions can have varying numbers of items, focusing
227	                           only on balancing the sum of sequence lengths.
228	
229	    Returns:
230	        List[List[int]]: A list containing k_partitions lists. Each inner list contains the
231	                         original indices of the items assigned to that partition. The indices
232	                         within each partition list are sorted.
233	
234	    Raises:
235	        AssertionError: If len(seqlen_list) < k_partitions.
236	        AssertionError: If equal_size is True and len(seqlen_list) is not divisible by k_partitions.
237	        AssertionError: If any resulting partition is empty.
238	    """
239	    assert len(seqlen_list) >= k_partitions, f"number of items:[{len(seqlen_list)}] < k_partitions:[{k_partitions}]"
240	
241	    def _check_and_sort_partitions(partitions):
242	        assert len(partitions) == k_partitions, f"{len(partitions)} != {k_partitions}"
243	        seen_idx = set()
244	        sorted_partitions = [None] * k_partitions
245	        for i, partition in enumerate(partitions):
246	            assert len(partition) > 0, f"the {i}-th partition is empty"
247	            for idx in partition:
248	                seen_idx.add(idx)
249	            sorted_partitions[i] = sorted(partition)
250	        assert seen_idx == set(range(len(seqlen_list)))
251	        return sorted_partitions
252	
253	    partitions = karmarkar_karp(seqlen_list=seqlen_list, k_partitions=k_partitions, equal_size=equal_size)
254	    return _check_and_sort_partitions(partitions)

257	def log_seqlen_unbalance(seqlen_list: list[int], partitions: list[list[int]], prefix):
258	    """
259	    Calculate and log metrics related to sequence length imbalance before and after partitioning.
260	
261	    Args:
262	        seqlen_list (List[int]): A list of sequence lengths for each item.
263	        partitions (List[List[int]]): A list of partitions, where each inner list contains indices
264	                                      from seqlen_list assigned to that partition.
265	        prefix (str): A prefix to be added to each metric key in the returned dictionary.
266	
267	    Returns:
268	        dict: A dictionary containing metrics related to sequence length imbalance.
269	    """
270	    # Get the number of partitions
271	    k_partition = len(partitions)
272	    # assert len(seqlen_list) % k_partition == 0
273	    batch_size = len(seqlen_list) // k_partition
274	    min_sum_seqlen = None
275	    max_sum_seqlen = None
276	    total_sum_seqlen = 0
277	
278	    # Iterate over each batch of sequence lengths
279	    for offset in range(0, len(seqlen_list), batch_size):
280	        cur_sum_seqlen = sum(seqlen_list[offset : offset + batch_size])
281	        if min_sum_seqlen is None or cur_sum_seqlen < min_sum_seqlen:
282	            min_sum_seqlen = cur_sum_seqlen
283	        if max_sum_seqlen is None or cur_sum_seqlen > max_sum_seqlen:
284	            max_sum_seqlen = cur_sum_seqlen
285	        total_sum_seqlen += cur_sum_seqlen
286	
287	    balanced_sum_seqlen_list = []
288	    for partition in partitions:
289	        cur_sum_seqlen_balanced = sum([seqlen_list[i] for i in partition])
290	        balanced_sum_seqlen_list.append(cur_sum_seqlen_balanced)
291	    # print("balanced_sum_seqlen_list: ", balanced_sum_seqlen_list)
292	    min_sum_seqlen_balanced = min(balanced_sum_seqlen_list)
293	    max_sum_seqlen_balanced = max(balanced_sum_seqlen_list)
294	
295	    return {
296	        f"{prefix}/min": min_sum_seqlen,
297	        f"{prefix}/max": max_sum_seqlen,
298	        f"{prefix}/minmax_diff": max_sum_seqlen - min_sum_seqlen,
299	        f"{prefix}/balanced_min": min_sum_seqlen_balanced,
300	        f"{prefix}/balanced_max": max_sum_seqlen_balanced,
301	        f"{prefix}/mean": total_sum_seqlen / len(partitions),
302	    }

305	def ceildiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:
306	    """Compute ceiling division of a by b.
307	
308	    Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to a/b.
309	    Uses the identity: ceil(a/b) = floor((a + b - 1) / b) = -(-a // b)
310	
311	    Args:
312	        a: Dividend (numerator).
313	        b: Divisor (denominator), must be non-zero.
314	
315	    Returns:
316	        int: Ceiling of a divided by b.
317	
318	    Example:
319	        >>> ceildiv(7, 3)  # ceil(7/3) = ceil(2.33) = 3
320	        3
321	        >>> ceildiv(6, 3)  # ceil(6/3) = ceil(2.0) = 2
322	        2
323	    """
324	    return -(a // -b)
325

327	def roundup_divisible(a: int, b: int) -> int:
328	    """Round up a to the nearest multiple of b.
329	
330	    Returns the smallest multiple of b that is >= a.
331	
332	    Args:
333	        a: Value to round up.
334	        b: Divisor to round to (must be positive).
335	
336	    Returns:
337	        int: Smallest multiple of b that is >= a.
338	
339	    Example:
340	        >>> roundup_divisible(7, 4)  # nearest multiple of 4 >= 7 is 8
341	        8
342	        >>> roundup_divisible(8, 4)  # 8 is already a multiple of 4
343	        8
344	    """
345	    return ((a + b - 1) // b) * b

348	def rearrange_micro_batches(
349	    batch,
350	    max_token_len,
351	    dp_group=None,
352	    num_batches_divided_by=None,
353	    same_micro_num_in_dp=True,
354	    min_num_micro_batch=None,
355	    use_dynamic_bsz_balance=True,
356	    force_group_size=1,
357	):
358	    """
359	    Split a batch into micro-batches by total token count, with optional DP sync and padding.
360	
361	    Args:
362	        batch (TensorDict): must include "attention_mask" (B*S); other fields are sliced similarly.
363	        max_token_len (int): max sum of attention_mask per micro-batch.
364	        dp_group (optional): torch.distributed group for data-parallel sync.
365	        num_batches_divided_by (optional): virtual pipeline parallel size, for megatron.
366	        same_micro_num_in_dp (bool): if True and dp_group set, pad all ranks to the same count.
367	        min_num_micro_batch (int, optional): force at least this many splits (pads empty ones).
368	        use_dynamic_bsz_balance (bool, optional): balance the computational workload between micro-batches
369	        force_group_size (int, optional): force consecutive samples to be in the same micro-batch (for RM training).
370	
371	    Returns:
372	        List[TensorDict]: the micro-batches.
373	        List[List[int]]: index lists mapping each micro-batch back to original positions.
374	    """
375	    # this is per local micro_bsz
376	    input_ids = batch["input_ids"]
377	    if input_ids.is_nested:
378	        seq_len_effective: torch.Tensor = input_ids.offsets().diff()
379	        max_seq_len = max(seq_len_effective)
380	    else:
381	        max_seq_len = batch["attention_mask"].shape[-1]
382	        seq_len_effective: torch.Tensor = batch["attention_mask"].sum(dim=1)
383	
384	    assert max_token_len >= max_seq_len, (
385	        f"max_token_len must be greater than the sequence length. Got {max_token_len=} and {max_seq_len=}"
386	    )
387	
388	    # Validate force_group_size
389	    batch_size = len(seq_len_effective)
390	    assert batch_size % force_group_size == 0, (
391	        f"Batch size {batch_size} must be divisible by force_group_size {force_group_size}"
392	    )
393	
394	    total_seqlen = seq_len_effective.sum().item()
395	    # NOTE: num_microbatches <= batch_size, so take the min of this two.
396	    # When force_group_size > 1, we work with groups instead of individual samples
397	    num_groups = batch_size // force_group_size
398	    num_micro_batches = min(num_groups, ceildiv(total_seqlen, max_token_len))
399	    if min_num_micro_batch is not None:
400	        # used to support pp
401	        num_micro_batches = max(min_num_micro_batch, num_micro_batches)
402	    if dist.is_initialized() and same_micro_num_in_dp and dp_group is not None:
403	        num_micro_batches = torch.tensor([num_micro_batches], device=get_device_name())
404	        dist.all_reduce(num_micro_batches, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX, group=dp_group)
405	        num_micro_batches = num_micro_batches.cpu().item()
406	    if num_batches_divided_by is not None:
407	        num_micro_batches = roundup_divisible(num_micro_batches, num_batches_divided_by)
408	
409	    assert num_micro_batches <= num_groups
410	
411	    # upcast to int64 to avoid potential overflow im `calculate_workload` computation.
412	    seq_len_effective = seq_len_effective.long()
413	
414	    # When force_group_size > 1, aggregate workloads by groups
415	    if force_group_size > 1:
416	        # Calculate workload for each group (sum of workloads of samples in the group)
417	        workloads_per_sample = calculate_workload(seq_len_effective)
418	        workloads_per_sample_grouped = workloads_per_sample.view(num_groups, force_group_size)
419	        group_workloads = workloads_per_sample_grouped.sum(dim=1).cpu().tolist()
420	
421	        # Partition groups instead of individual samples
422	        micro_bsz_group_idx = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(group_workloads, num_micro_batches, equal_size=False)
423	
424	        # Convert group indices back to sample indices
425	        micro_bsz_idx = []
426	        for group_partition in micro_bsz_group_idx:
427	            sample_partition = []
428	            for group_idx in group_partition:
429	                start_idx = group_idx * force_group_size
430	                sample_partition.extend(range(start_idx, start_idx + force_group_size))
431	            micro_bsz_idx.append(sample_partition)
432	
433	        workloads = group_workloads
434	    else:
435	        # Original logic for force_group_size == 1
436	        # note that seq_len_effective is a GPU tensor. We need to make it a list to avoid D2H!
437	        workloads = calculate_workload(seq_len_effective).cpu().tolist()
438	        micro_bsz_idx = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(workloads, num_micro_batches, equal_size=False)
439	
440	    if use_dynamic_bsz_balance:
441	        # Use the sum of squared sequence lengths to approximate attention computation workload
442	        if force_group_size > 1:
443	            # For grouped samples, use group workloads for sorting
444	            micro_bsz_idx.sort(
445	                key=lambda partition: (
446	                    sum(workloads[idx // force_group_size] for idx in partition[::force_group_size]),
447	                    partition[0] if partition else 0,
448	                ),
449	                reverse=True,
450	            )
451	        else:
452	            micro_bsz_idx.sort(
453	                key=lambda partition: (
454	                    sum(workloads[idx] for idx in partition),
455	                    partition[0] if partition else 0,
456	                ),
457	                reverse=True,
458	            )
459	        # Place smaller micro-batches at both ends to reduce the bubbles exposed during the warm-up and cool-down.
460	        micro_bsz_idx = micro_bsz_idx[::2][::-1] + micro_bsz_idx[1::2]
461	
462	    micro_batches = []
463	
464	    for partition in micro_bsz_idx:
465	        curr_micro_batch = tu.index_select_tensor_dict(batch, partition)
466	        micro_batches.append(curr_micro_batch)
467	
468	    return micro_batches, micro_bsz_idx

471	def get_reverse_idx(idx_map):
472	    """
473	    Build the inverse of an index mapping.
474	
475	    Args:
476	        idx_map (Sequence[int]): Sequence where idx_map[i] = j.
477	
478	    Returns:
479	        List[int]: Inverse mapping list such that output[j] = i for each i.
480	    """
481	    reverse_idx_map = copy.deepcopy(idx_map)
482	
483	    for i, idx in enumerate(idx_map):
484	        reverse_idx_map[idx] = i
485	
486	    return reverse_idx_map

489	def prepare_dynamic_batch(
490	    data: DataProto,
491	    max_token_len: int,
492	    dp_group=None,
493	    num_batches_divided_by=None,
494	    same_micro_num_in_dp=True,
495	    min_num_micro_batch=None,
496	    use_dynamic_bsz_balance=True,
497	) -> tuple[list[DataProto], list[list[int]]]:
498	    """
499	    Prepare a batch for dynamic batching.
500	
501	    Args:
502	        data (DataProto): The input data.
503	        max_token_len (int): The maximum token length for dynamic batching.
504	
505	    Returns:
506	        Tuple[List[DataProto], List[List[int]]]: A tuple containing a list of DataProto objects
507	        and a list of index lists.
508	    """
509	    batch, batch_idx_list = rearrange_micro_batches(
510	        data.batch,
511	        max_token_len=max_token_len,
512	        dp_group=dp_group,
513	        num_batches_divided_by=num_batches_divided_by,
514	        same_micro_num_in_dp=same_micro_num_in_dp,
515	        min_num_micro_batch=min_num_micro_batch,
516	        use_dynamic_bsz_balance=use_dynamic_bsz_balance,
517	    )
518	    micro_batches = []
519	    for i, batch_idx in enumerate(batch_idx_list):
520	        tensors = dict(batch[i])
521	        non_tensors = {key: value[batch_idx] for key, value in data.non_tensor_batch.items()}
522	        meta_info = copy.deepcopy(data.meta_info)
523	        micro_batches.append(DataProto.from_dict(tensors, non_tensors, meta_info=meta_info))
524	
525	    return micro_batches, batch_idx_list

528	def restore_dynamic_batch(data: torch.Tensor, batch_idx_list: list[list[int]]) -> torch.Tensor:
529	    """
530	    Restore a batch from dynamic batching.
531	
532	    Args:
533	        data (torch.Tensor): The input data.
534	        batch_idx_list (List[List[int]]): The list of index lists.
535	
536	    Returns:
537	        torch.Tensor: The restored data.
538	    """
539	    indices = list(chain.from_iterable(batch_idx_list))
540	    batch_size = data.shape[0]
541	    assert len(indices) == batch_size, f"{len(indices)} vs. {batch_size}"
542	    revert_indices = torch.tensor(get_reverse_idx(indices), dtype=torch.long)
543	
544	    if data.is_nested:
545	        data_lst = data.unbind()
546	        tensors = [data_lst[i] for i in revert_indices]
547	        reverted_data = torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(tensors, layout=torch.jagged)
548	    else:
549	        reverted_data = data[revert_indices]
550	
551	    return reverted_data

27	def calculate_workload(seqlen_list: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
28	    """Calculate approximate computational workload for transformer attention.
29	
30	    Estimates FLOPs for dense transformer blocks based on sequence length using
31	    the formula: FLOPs ≈ 12 * hidden_size² * seqlen + 2 * hidden_size * seqlen²
32	
33	    The constants are calibrated for a 7B model (hidden_size=4096), yielding:
34	    workload ∝ 24576 * seqlen + seqlen²
35	
36	    Args:
37	        seqlen_list: Sequence lengths as a tensor.
38	
39	    Returns:
40	        torch.Tensor: Estimated workload values proportional to actual FLOPs.
41	
42	    Note:
43	        The returned values are relative workloads, not actual FLOP counts.
44	        Useful for balancing computation across data parallel ranks.
45	    """
46	    return 24576 * seqlen_list + seqlen_list**2

49	def karmarkar_karp(seqlen_list: list[int], k_partitions: int, equal_size: bool) -> list[list[int]]:
50	    """Partition items into k groups using the Karmarkar-Karp differencing method.
51	
52	    Implements the Largest Differencing Method (LDM) algorithm for balanced
53	    multi-way number partitioning. This heuristic produces near-optimal partitions
54	    by iteratively combining the sets with the largest difference.
55	
56	    Args:
57	        seqlen_list: Values to partition (typically sequence lengths or workloads).
58	        k_partitions: Number of partitions to create.
59	        equal_size: If True, each partition will have exactly len(seqlen_list) / k_partitions
60	            items. If False, partitions may have different sizes.
61	
62	    Returns:
63	        list[list[int]]: List of k partitions, each containing indices into seqlen_list.
64	
65	    See Also:
66	        https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largest_differencing_method
67	
68	    Note:
69	        When equal_size=True, len(seqlen_list) must be divisible by k_partitions.
70	    """
71	
72	    # see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largest_differencing_method
73	    class Set:
74	        def __init__(self) -> None:
75	            self.sum = 0
76	            self.items = []
77	
78	        def add(self, idx: int, val: int):
79	            self.items.append((idx, val))
80	            self.sum += val
81	
82	        def merge(self, other):
83	            for idx, val in other.items:
84	                self.items.append((idx, val))
85	                self.sum += val
86	
87	        def __lt__(self, other):
88	            if self.sum != other.sum:
89	                return self.sum < other.sum
90	            if len(self.items) != len(other.items):
91	                return len(self.items) < len(other.items)
92	            return self.items < other.items
93	
94	    class State:
95	        def __init__(self, items: list[tuple[int, int]], k: int) -> None:
96	            self.k = k
97	            # sets should always be decreasing order
98	            self.sets = [Set() for _ in range(k)]
99	            assert len(items) in [1, k], f"{len(items)} not in [1, {k}]"
100	            for i, (idx, seqlen) in enumerate(items):
101	                self.sets[i].add(idx=idx, val=seqlen)
102	            self.sets = sorted(self.sets, reverse=True)
103	
104	        def get_partitions(self):
105	            partitions = []
106	            for i in range(len(self.sets)):
107	                cur_partition = []
108	                for idx, _ in self.sets[i].items:
109	                    cur_partition.append(idx)
110	                partitions.append(cur_partition)
111	            return partitions
112	
113	        def merge(self, other):
114	            for i in range(self.k):
115	                self.sets[i].merge(other.sets[self.k - 1 - i])
116	            self.sets = sorted(self.sets, reverse=True)
117	
118	        @property
119	        def spread(self) -> int:
120	            return self.sets[0].sum - self.sets[-1].sum
121	
122	        def __lt__(self, other):
123	            # least heap, let the state with largest spread to be popped first,
124	            # if the spread is the same, let the state who has the largest set
125	            # to be popped first.
126	            if self.spread != other.spread:
127	                return self.spread > other.spread
128	            return self.sets[0] > other.sets[0]
129	
130	        def __repr__(self) -> str:
131	            repr_str = "["
132	            for i in range(self.k):
133	                if i > 0:
134	                    repr_str += ","
135	                repr_str += "{"
136	                for j, (_, seqlen) in enumerate(self.sets[i].items):
137	                    if j > 0:
138	                        repr_str += ","
139	                    repr_str += str(seqlen)
140	                repr_str += "}"
141	            repr_str += "]"
142	            return repr_str
143	
144	    sorted_seqlen_list = sorted([(seqlen, i) for i, seqlen in enumerate(seqlen_list)])
145	    states_pq = []
146	    if equal_size:
147	        assert len(seqlen_list) % k_partitions == 0, f"{len(seqlen_list)} % {k_partitions} != 0"
148	        for offset in range(0, len(sorted_seqlen_list), k_partitions):
149	            items = []
150	            for i in range(k_partitions):
151	                seqlen, idx = sorted_seqlen_list[offset + i]
152	                items.append((idx, seqlen))
153	            heapq.heappush(states_pq, State(items=items, k=k_partitions))
154	    else:
155	        for seqlen, idx in sorted_seqlen_list:
156	            heapq.heappush(states_pq, State(items=[(idx, seqlen)], k=k_partitions))
157	
158	    while len(states_pq) > 1:
159	        state0 = heapq.heappop(states_pq)
160	        state1 = heapq.heappop(states_pq)
161	        # merge states
162	        state0.merge(state1)
163	        heapq.heappush(states_pq, state0)
164	
165	    final_state = states_pq[0]
166	    partitions = final_state.get_partitions()
167	    if equal_size:
168	        for i, partition in enumerate(partitions):
169	            assert len(partition) * k_partitions == len(seqlen_list), (
170	                f"{len(partition)} * {k_partitions} != {len(seqlen_list)}"
171	            )
172	    return partitions

175	def greedy_partition(seqlen_list: list[int], k_partitions: int, equal_size: bool) -> list[list[int]]:
176	    """Partition items into k groups using a greedy assignment strategy.
177	
178	    Assigns each item to the partition with the smallest current sum, iterating
179	    through items in order. Simpler but typically less optimal than Karmarkar-Karp.
180	
181	    Args:
182	        seqlen_list: Values to partition (typically sequence lengths or workloads).
183	        k_partitions: Number of partitions to create.
184	        equal_size: If True, adds a bias to ensure equal partition sizes.
185	            Requires len(seqlen_list) to be divisible by k_partitions.
186	
187	    Returns:
188	        list[list[int]]: List of k partitions, each containing indices into seqlen_list.
189	
190	    Note:
191	        When equal_size=True, a large bias is added to encourage equal distribution
192	        of items before considering the actual values.
193	    """
194	    bias = sum(seqlen_list) + 1 if equal_size else 0
195	    sorted_seqlen = [(seqlen + bias, i) for i, seqlen in enumerate(seqlen_list)]
196	    partitions = [[] for _ in range(k_partitions)]
197	    partition_sums = [0 for _ in range(k_partitions)]
198	    for seqlen, i in sorted_seqlen:
199	        min_idx = None
200	        for j in range(k_partitions):
201	            if min_idx is None or partition_sums[j] < partition_sums[min_idx]:
202	                min_idx = j
203	        partitions[min_idx].append(i)
204	        partition_sums[min_idx] += seqlen
205	    if equal_size:
206	        for i, partition in enumerate(partitions):
207	            assert len(partition) * k_partitions == len(seqlen_list), (
208	                f"{len(partition)} * {k_partitions} != {len(seqlen_list)}"
209	            )
210	    return partitions

213	def get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(seqlen_list: list[int], k_partitions: int, equal_size: bool):
214	    """
215	    Calculates partitions of indices from seqlen_list such that the sum of sequence lengths
216	    in each partition is balanced. Uses the Karmarkar-Karp differencing method.
217	
218	    This is useful for balancing workload across devices or batches, especially when
219	    dealing with variable sequence lengths.
220	
221	    Args:
222	        seqlen_list (List[int]): A list of sequence lengths for each item.
223	        k_partitions (int): The desired number of partitions.
224	        equal_size (bool): If True, ensures that each partition has the same number of items.
225	                           Requires len(seqlen_list) to be divisible by k_partitions.
226	                           If False, partitions can have varying numbers of items, focusing
227	                           only on balancing the sum of sequence lengths.
228	
229	    Returns:
230	        List[List[int]]: A list containing k_partitions lists. Each inner list contains the
231	                         original indices of the items assigned to that partition. The indices
232	                         within each partition list are sorted.
233	
234	    Raises:
235	        AssertionError: If len(seqlen_list) < k_partitions.
236	        AssertionError: If equal_size is True and len(seqlen_list) is not divisible by k_partitions.
237	        AssertionError: If any resulting partition is empty.
238	    """
239	    assert len(seqlen_list) >= k_partitions, f"number of items:[{len(seqlen_list)}] < k_partitions:[{k_partitions}]"
240	
241	    def _check_and_sort_partitions(partitions):
242	        assert len(partitions) == k_partitions, f"{len(partitions)} != {k_partitions}"
243	        seen_idx = set()
244	        sorted_partitions = [None] * k_partitions
245	        for i, partition in enumerate(partitions):
246	            assert len(partition) > 0, f"the {i}-th partition is empty"
247	            for idx in partition:
248	                seen_idx.add(idx)
249	            sorted_partitions[i] = sorted(partition)
250	        assert seen_idx == set(range(len(seqlen_list)))
251	        return sorted_partitions
252	
253	    partitions = karmarkar_karp(seqlen_list=seqlen_list, k_partitions=k_partitions, equal_size=equal_size)
254	    return _check_and_sort_partitions(partitions)

305	def ceildiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:
306	    """Compute ceiling division of a by b.
307	
308	    Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to a/b.
309	    Uses the identity: ceil(a/b) = floor((a + b - 1) / b) = -(-a // b)
310	
311	    Args:
312	        a: Dividend (numerator).
313	        b: Divisor (denominator), must be non-zero.
314	
315	    Returns:
316	        int: Ceiling of a divided by b.
317	
318	    Example:
319	        >>> ceildiv(7, 3)  # ceil(7/3) = ceil(2.33) = 3
320	        3
321	        >>> ceildiv(6, 3)  # ceil(6/3) = ceil(2.0) = 2
322	        2
323	    """
324	    return -(a // -b)

327	def roundup_divisible(a: int, b: int) -> int:
328	    """Round up a to the nearest multiple of b.
329	
330	    Returns the smallest multiple of b that is >= a.
331	
332	    Args:
333	        a: Value to round up.
334	        b: Divisor to round to (must be positive).
335	
336	    Returns:
337	        int: Smallest multiple of b that is >= a.
338	
339	    Example:
340	        >>> roundup_divisible(7, 4)  # nearest multiple of 4 >= 7 is 8
341	        8
342	        >>> roundup_divisible(8, 4)  # 8 is already a multiple of 4
343	        8
344	    """
345	    return ((a + b - 1) // b) * b

348	def rearrange_micro_batches(
349	    batch,
350	    max_token_len,
351	    dp_group=None,
352	    num_batches_divided_by=None,
353	    same_micro_num_in_dp=True,
354	    min_num_micro_batch=None,
355	    use_dynamic_bsz_balance=True,

359	    Split a batch into micro-batches by total token count, with optional DP sync and padding.
360	
361	    Args:
362	        batch (TensorDict): must include "attention_mask" (B*S); other fields are sliced similarly.
363	        max_token_len (int): max sum of attention_mask per micro-batch.
364	        dp_group (optional): torch.distributed group for data-parallel sync.
365	        num_batches_divided_by (optional): virtual pipeline parallel size, for megatron.
366	        same_micro_num_in_dp (bool): if True and dp_group set, pad all ranks to the same count.
367	        min_num_micro_batch (int, optional): force at least this many splits (pads empty ones).
368	        use_dynamic_bsz_balance (bool, optional): balance the computational workload between micro-batches
369	        force_group_size (int, optional): force consecutive samples to be in the same micro-batch (for RM training).
370	
371	    Returns:
372	        List[TensorDict]: the micro-batches.
373	        List[List[int]]: index lists mapping each micro-batch back to original positions.
374	    """
375	    # this is per local micro_bsz
376	    input_ids = batch["input_ids"]
377	    if input_ids.is_nested:
378	        seq_len_effective: torch.Tensor = input_ids.offsets().diff()
379	        max_seq_len = max(seq_len_effective)
380	    else:
381	        max_seq_len = batch["attention_mask"].shape[-1]
382	        seq_len_effective: torch.Tensor = batch["attention_mask"].sum(dim=1)
383	
384	    assert max_token_len >= max_seq_len, (
385	        f"max_token_len must be greater than the sequence length. Got {max_token_len=} and {max_seq_len=}"
386	    )
387	
388	    # Validate force_group_size
389	    batch_size = len(seq_len_effective)
390	    assert batch_size % force_group_size == 0, (
391	        f"Batch size {batch_size} must be divisible by force_group_size {force_group_size}"
392	    )
393	
394	    total_seqlen = seq_len_effective.sum().item()
395	    # NOTE: num_microbatches <= batch_size, so take the min of this two.
396	    # When force_group_size > 1, we work with groups instead of individual samples
397	    num_groups = batch_size // force_group_size
398	    num_micro_batches = min(num_groups, ceildiv(total_seqlen, max_token_len))
399	    if min_num_micro_batch is not None:
400	        # used to support pp
401	        num_micro_batches = max(min_num_micro_batch, num_micro_batches)
402	    if dist.is_initialized() and same_micro_num_in_dp and dp_group is not None:
403	        num_micro_batches = torch.tensor([num_micro_batches], device=get_device_name())
404	        dist.all_reduce(num_micro_batches, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX, group=dp_group)
405	        num_micro_batches = num_micro_batches.cpu().item()
406	    if num_batches_divided_by is not None:
407	        num_micro_batches = roundup_divisible(num_micro_batches, num_batches_divided_by)
408	
409	    assert num_micro_batches <= num_groups
410	
411	    # upcast to int64 to avoid potential overflow im `calculate_workload` computation.
412	    seq_len_effective = seq_len_effective.long()
413	
414	    # When force_group_size > 1, aggregate workloads by groups
415	    if force_group_size > 1:
416	        # Calculate workload for each group (sum of workloads of samples in the group)
417	        workloads_per_sample = calculate_workload(seq_len_effective)
418	        workloads_per_sample_grouped = workloads_per_sample.view(num_groups, force_group_size)
419	        group_workloads = workloads_per_sample_grouped.sum(dim=1).cpu().tolist()
420	
421	        # Partition groups instead of individual samples
422	        micro_bsz_group_idx = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(group_workloads, num_micro_batches, equal_size=False)
423	
424	        # Convert group indices back to sample indices
425	        micro_bsz_idx = []
426	        for group_partition in micro_bsz_group_idx:
427	            sample_partition = []
428	            for group_idx in group_partition:
429	                start_idx = group_idx * force_group_size
430	                sample_partition.extend(range(start_idx, start_idx + force_group_size))
431	            micro_bsz_idx.append(sample_partition)
432	
433	        workloads = group_workloads
434	    else:
435	        # Original logic for force_group_size == 1
436	        # note that seq_len_effective is a GPU tensor. We need to make it a list to avoid D2H!
437	        workloads = calculate_workload(seq_len_effective).cpu().tolist()
438	        micro_bsz_idx = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(workloads, num_micro_batches, equal_size=False)
439	
440	    if use_dynamic_bsz_balance:
441	        # Use the sum of squared sequence lengths to approximate attention computation workload
442	        if force_group_size > 1:
443	            # For grouped samples, use group workloads for sorting
444	            micro_bsz_idx.sort(
445	                key=lambda partition: (
446	                    sum(workloads[idx // force_group_size] for idx in partition[::force_group_size]),
447	                    partition[0] if partition else 0,
448	                ),
449	                reverse=True,
450	            )
451	        else:
452	            micro_bsz_idx.sort(
453	                key=lambda partition: (
454	                    sum(workloads[idx] for idx in partition),
455	                    partition[0] if partition else 0,
456	                ),

458	            )
459	        # Place smaller micro-batches at both ends to reduce the bubbles exposed during the warm-up and cool-down.
460	        micro_bsz_idx = micro_bsz_idx[::2][::-1] + micro_bsz_idx[1::2]
461	
462	    micro_batches = []
463	
464	    for partition in micro_bsz_idx:
465	        curr_micro_batch = tu.index_select_tensor_dict(batch, partition)
466	        micro_batches.append(curr_micro_batch)
467	
468	    return micro_batches, micro_bsz_idx

499	    Prepare a batch for dynamic batching.
500	
501	    Args:
502	        data (DataProto): The input data.
503	        max_token_len (int): The maximum token length for dynamic batching.
504	
505	    Returns:
506	        Tuple[List[DataProto], List[List[int]]]: A tuple containing a list of DataProto objects
507	        and a list of index lists.
508	    """
509	    batch, batch_idx_list = rearrange_micro_batches(
510	        data.batch,
511	        max_token_len=max_token_len,
512	        dp_group=dp_group,
513	        num_batches_divided_by=num_batches_divided_by,
514	        same_micro_num_in_dp=same_micro_num_in_dp,
515	        min_num_micro_batch=min_num_micro_batch,
516	        use_dynamic_bsz_balance=use_dynamic_bsz_balance,
517	    )
518	    micro_batches = []
519	    for i, batch_idx in enumerate(batch_idx_list):
520	        tensors = dict(batch[i])
521	        non_tensors = {key: value[batch_idx] for key, value in data.non_tensor_batch.items()}
522	        meta_info = copy.deepcopy(data.meta_info)
523	        micro_batches.append(DataProto.from_dict(tensors, non_tensors, meta_info=meta_info))
524	
525	    return micro_batches, batch_idx_list

528	def restore_dynamic_batch(data: torch.Tensor, batch_idx_list: list[list[int]]) -> torch.Tensor:
529	    """
530	    Restore a batch from dynamic batching.
531	
532	    Args:
533	        data (torch.Tensor): The input data.
534	        batch_idx_list (List[List[int]]): The list of index lists.
535	
536	    Returns:
537	        torch.Tensor: The restored data.
538	    """
539	    indices = list(chain.from_iterable(batch_idx_list))
540	    batch_size = data.shape[0]
541	    assert len(indices) == batch_size, f"{len(indices)} vs. {batch_size}"
542	    revert_indices = torch.tensor(get_reverse_idx(indices), dtype=torch.long)
543	
544	    if data.is_nested:
545	        data_lst = data.unbind()
546	        tensors = [data_lst[i] for i in revert_indices]
547	        reverted_data = torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(tensors, layout=torch.jagged)
548	    else:
549	        reverted_data = data[revert_indices]
550	
551	    return reverted_data
552	
553	
554	def get_group_balanced_partitions(
555	    seqlen_list: list[int],
556	    uid_list: list,
557	    k_partitions: int,
558	) -> list[list[int]]:
559	    """
560	    Partition samples into k groups while keeping samples with the same uid together.
561	
562	    Args:
563	        seqlen_list: List of sequence lengths for each sample.
564	        uid_list: List of uids identifying which samples share the same prefix.
565	                  Samples with the same uid will be kept together.
566	        k_partitions: Number of partitions (typically world_size).
567	
568	    Returns:
569	        List of k lists, each containing sample indices assigned to that partition.
570	        Samples with the same uid are guaranteed to be in the same partition.
571	    """
572	    assert len(seqlen_list) == len(uid_list), "seqlen_list and uid_list must have same length"
573	
574	    # Build groups: each group contains indices of samples with the same uid
575	    # Assumes samples with same uid are contiguous
576	    groups = []  # List of (group_indices, group_total_seqlen)
577	    current_uid = None
578	    current_indices = []
579	    current_seqlen = 0
580	
581	    for i, (seqlen, uid) in enumerate(zip(seqlen_list, uid_list, strict=False)):
582	        if uid != current_uid:
583	            if current_indices:
584	                groups.append((current_indices, current_seqlen))
585	            current_uid = uid
586	            current_indices = [i]
587	            current_seqlen = seqlen
588	        else:
589	            current_indices.append(i)
590	            current_seqlen += seqlen
591	
592	    # Don't forget the last group
593	    if current_indices:
594	        groups.append((current_indices, current_seqlen))
595	
596	    num_groups = len(groups)
597	    assert num_groups >= k_partitions, (
598	        f"Number of uid groups ({num_groups}) must be >= k_partitions ({k_partitions}). "
599	        f"Consider reducing world_size or increasing batch_size."
600	    )
601	
602	    # Calculate workload for each group (as integers for partitioning)
603	    group_workloads = []
604	    for indices, total_seqlen in groups:
605	        # Use sum of individual workloads for more accurate estimation
606	        workload = sum(int(calculate_workload(torch.tensor([seqlen_list[i]])).item()) for i in indices)
607	        group_workloads.append(workload)
608	
609	    # Use Karmarkar-Karp to partition groups
610	    # equal_size=True ensures each partition gets the same number of groups,
611	    # which is required when each group has the same number of samples (rollout.n)
612	    group_partitions = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(
613	        seqlen_list=group_workloads,
614	        k_partitions=k_partitions,
615	        equal_size=True,
616	    )
617	
618	    # Convert group partitions to sample partitions
619	    sample_partitions = []
620	    for group_partition in group_partitions:
621	        sample_indices = []
622	        for group_idx in group_partition:

624	        sample_partitions.append(sorted(sample_indices))
